content.user_title: Build Azure Cosmos DB Java Workflows
content.value_statement: Java teams need reliable patterns for Cosmos DB setup, authentication, CRUD, and query work. This skill provides focused Java SDK guidance for clients, containers, async flows, RU awareness, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Shows Maven dependency setup for the Azure Cosmos DB Java SDK.
Explains client creation with endpoint and key configuration.
Covers synchronous and asynchronous client patterns.
Demonstrates database, container, item, and query workflows.
Summarizes partition key, consistency level, RU, and retry concepts.
Links to official package, documentation, samples, and troubleshooting resources.
limitations: Does not provision Azure resources or manage cloud permissions.
Does not validate account-specific throughput, indexing, or region settings.
Requires users to protect credentials and test code in their own environment.
Focuses on the NoSQL API and Java SDK examples only.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Cosmos DB Java Service
use_cases.description: Create a working Java service flow for clients, databases, containers, and item operations.

use_cases.title: Review Async Database Patterns
use_cases.description: Compare synchronous and asynchronous SDK usage before choosing a production access pattern.

use_cases.title: Prepare Operational Guidance
use_cases.description: Document partition key, consistency, RU, retry, and troubleshooting considerations for a team.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Client
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a Java application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create an Azure Cosmos DB Java client using environment variables for the endpoint and key. Explain each setup step.

prompt_templates.title: Add CRUD Operations
prompt_templates.scenario: Build item workflows for a simple domain object.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Java Cosmos DB workflow that creates a database, creates a container, and performs create, read, update, and delete operations.

prompt_templates.title: Use Async Patterns
prompt_templates.scenario: Move a service path to reactive SDK usage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert my Cosmos DB Java workflow to use the async client. Include chaining, subscription handling, and clear error handling guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Cosmos DB Java configuration for partition keys, consistency, preferred regions, direct mode, RU usage, and 429 retry behavior.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to connect a Java service to Cosmos DB.
output_examples.output: A setup plan covering the Maven dependency, endpoint and key configuration, client creation, and safe credential handling.

output_examples.input: A team needs CRUD guidance for a new container.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline for database creation, container creation, item creation, reads, updates, deletes, and partition key usage.

output_examples.input: An architect wants to improve production readiness.
output_examples.output: A review checklist for async usage, preferred regions, direct mode, consistency, RU charge visibility, and retry handling.

best_practices: Reuse CosmosClient instances instead of creating a new client per operation.
Choose partition keys with high cardinality and even request distribution.
Track RU charges and handle 429 responses with retry-aware application logic.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode account keys or endpoints in source code.
Do not choose low-cardinality partition keys for high-volume containers.
Do not block reactive flows without checking throughput and latency impact.

faq.question: Does this skill create Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It provides Java SDK guidance and examples. You must create and configure Azure resources separately.

faq.question: Which Cosmos DB API does it cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on the Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL API with the Java SDK.

faq.question: Can it help with async Java code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for CosmosAsyncClient, reactive chaining, and subscription patterns.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: It shows environment variable based credential loading. Users must still secure keys, rotate secrets, and limit access.

faq.question: Can it tune production performance?
faq.answer: It explains important topics like partition keys, RUs, direct mode, regions, and retries. Production tuning still needs workload testing.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
